primary.poolable_reason: TWO TRIALS WITH DIFFERENT ACTIVE COMPARATORS, AND THIS ONE IS GENUINELY ARGUABLE. Read from ClinicalTrials.gov 2026-08-18. NCT01844856 randomises eravacycline against ERTAPENEM (cure 191/220 against 198/226); NCT02784704 randomises it against MEROPENEM (177/195 against 187/205). Both are complicated intra-abdominal infection, both register clinical response at test-of-cure, both post clean counts. THE ONLY THING THAT DIFFERS IS THE COMPARATOR DRUG -- and both comparators are CARBAPENEMS. AUTHORITY: MECIR Box 10.10.a C62 -- 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

primary.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that any trial here is poor -- each is registered and reports its own primary. NOT that the drug is ineffective. NOT that no poolable question exists in this area: only that the question this page's title asks cannot be answered by pooling the trials this page carries. THE CRITICISM IS OF THE POOLING AND OF NOTHING ELSE. Registry read 2026-08-18.
primary.the_argument_both_ways_because_this_is_a: FOR CLOSING: different comparator, different question. Ertapenem and meropenem differ in spectrum and dosing, and the same rule closed AZILSARTAN, MENACYW and LENACAPAVIR. Applying it inconsistently to save a pool would be the worse error. FOR KEEPING: both are carbapenems used as the standard active control in the same infection, which is arguably 'sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful'. This is the MALARIA_ACT shape pointed at comparators rather than populations -- differing strings that may describe one question.
primary.why_it_is_referred_rather_than_decided: THE CONSERVATIVE OPTION IS THE ONE THAT DOES NOT MOVE A RESULT TOWARD SIGNIFICANCE BY OUR OWN DECISION. Here the two directions are not symmetric in cost: closing destroys a possibly legitimate synthesis, pooling publishes a possibly incoherent one. NO POOL IS DISPLAYED PENDING THE DECISION -- which is the conservative act -- but the topic is NOT recorded as settled, because it is not. Whether two carbapenem comparators count as one comparison is a scope decision about this corpus and it belongs to Mahmood.
primary.the_counts_are_recorded_so_the_decision_: If the decision is to pool: NCT01844856 191/220 against 198/226; NCT02784704 177/195 against 187/205; both clinical cure at test-of-cure. Nothing further needs reading.
primary.the_evidence_that_would_settle_it_rather: THE DECIDING QUESTION IS WHETHER A GUIDELINE OR REGULATOR TREATS ERTAPENEM AND MEROPENEM AS ONE COMPARATOR CLASS FOR COMPLICATED INTRA-ABDOMINAL INFECTION. If a regulatory review of the eravacycline programme, an FDA or EMA guidance on cIAI trial design, or a society guideline treats carbapenems as a single acceptable active control for this indication, THAT IS EVIDENCE FOR THE DECISION RATHER THAN AN OPINION ABOUT IT -- the same discipline as citing the Handbook instead of reasoning from first principles. NOTHING OF THE KIND HAS BEEN READ. It is recorded as the specific document to look for, so that whoever decides is deciding on a source rather than on plausibility. NOTE that the two are NOT clinically interchangeable in general -- ertapenem lacks reliable antipseudomonal activity and meropenem has it -- so the question is specifically whether that difference matters IN A CONTROL ARM for this infection, not whether they are the same drug.
